questions.q: What hard networking requirement does Managed Instance have that Azure SQL Database does not need in the same way?
options: A second logical server for failover
A dedicated subnet inside a Virtual Network, delegated specifically to Managed Instance
An ExpressRoute circuit to an on-prem datacenter
A public IP address with no firewall restrictions
questions.explain: This delegated subnet is a precondition for creation, not optional configuration you can add later.

questions.q: Roughly how long does provisioning a new Managed Instance commonly take?
options: A minute or two, same as Azure SQL Database
Four to six hours, sometimes longer
Exactly 24 hours, always
Under 10 seconds
questions.explain: This is the real, often-surprising provisioning time for the infrastructure behind Managed Instance's near-full SQL Server surface with PaaS patching.

questions.q: What does a "deployment-in-progress" status for several hours during Managed Instance creation indicate?
options: Normal, expected behavior — not an error or a stuck deployment
A subscription-level quota problem
A sign that the VNet subnet was misconfigured
A failed deployment that should be deleted and retried immediately
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns not to assume a deployment still running after twenty minutes has failed.

questions.q: What should a DBA do while a Managed Instance deployment runs for hours, per this lesson?
options: Confirm the subnet has no conflicting resources, prepare firewall/NSG rules ahead of time, and draft the migration plan — not delete and retry out of impatience
Manually SSH into the underlying VM to speed up provisioning
Nothing can be prepared in advance; all planning must wait until deployment completes
Repeatedly delete and recreate the instance until it deploys faster
questions.explain: There's nothing to click or fix during provisioning — the useful DBA work is preparing the next steps.

questions.q: Why does Managed Instance require the VNet subnet before creation rather than allowing it to be added afterward like an Azure SQL Database firewall rule?
options: Because Azure SQL Database also requires a VNet subnet before creation, identically
Because Microsoft has no technical way to add networking to any Azure resource after creation
Because Managed Instance's near-100% SQL Server surface area depends on network isolation that a shared, multi-tenant database model can't offer, making it a precondition for creation
Because subnets are only used for cost tracking, not actual isolation
questions.explain: This is the structural reason the VNet/subnet requirement is baked into Managed Instance's creation flow rather than being optional add-on configuration.
